Title: Histoire ecclesiastique des Eglises Reformees, recueillies en quelques Valees de Piedmont, et circonuoisines, autrefois appelees Eglises Vaudoises, commencant des l'an 1160 de nostre Seigneur, et finissant en l'an mil six cents quarante trois (the first printing, Geneva 1644; with two indices, one of the chapter summaries with their years and one of the matters)
Creator: Pierre Gilles (1571-1646 per the host catalogue), 'Pasteur de l'Eglise Reformee de la Tour' as the title page reads
Publisher: A Geneve: pour Iean de Tournes, Imprimeur ordinaire de la Republique et Academie (title page read in the OCR)
Publication Date: 1644 (title page read in the OCR as 'M. DC. XLIV' with noise; host catalogue 1644)
Rights: Public Domain (a seventeenth-century print carrying a Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0 on the host item; public domain by date under the project's 95-year rule)
Language: fra
Source: Internet Archive item bub_gb_v8j3OAjFNOoC, file bub_gb_v8j3OAjFNOoC_djvu.txt (a Google Books scan of the National Central Library of Rome copy, stamped 'Ex Bibliotheca majori Coll. Rom. Societ. Jesu'; collection europeanlibraries), fetched directly (curl, raw bytes) by the library/source-research thread (Era VII session, second-pass agent for the continental Reformed and Scandinavian worlds), 2026-10-23; host rights statement: licenseurl http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark); not access-restricted. A second scan of a 1655 Geneva printing (Jaques Remondet) is item bub_gb_3bpEABVwNjwC, same Public Domain Mark, sampled at five points and about as poorly read; not vendored.
Provenance note: Header prepended; the OCR text follows unchanged (no characters altered; the raw file contains 0 long-s glyphs, so no long-s normalisation was done). Rights basis restated: a seventeenth-century print carrying a Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0 on the host item; public domain by date under the project's 95-year rule.
Content note: The first printing of the work vendored in the clean 1881 Pignerol re-edition (gilles_histoire-ecclesiastique-eglises-vaudoises-v1-fra_1881.txt and -v2-). This file exists so that a quote taken from the 1881 text can be checked against the first printing's own spelling and wording; it is not the working text. The OCR preserves the dedication 'A Messieurs mes tres-honores et tres-chers freres en nostre Seigneur, les Pasteurs, Anciens, Diacres et autres Directeurs' of the valleys' churches (from about file line 60) and the running narrative from 1160 to 1643, but it catches none of the chapter headings (no 'CHAP.' line survives), so a passage is found here by searching a distinctive phrase from the 1881 text (spelling the old way: 'u' for 'v', 'f' for long s) rather than by chapter. The 1532 synod at Angrogna and the confirmation of its conclusion appear around file line 2831. The two indices the title promises are at the end of the volume. Chapter numbers and the year-marked summaries are in the 1881 edition. OCR sampled at 10/30/50/70/90 percent (about 0.69 of tokens read as words against a clean modern-French baseline of 0.92): the 1644 typography's long s is read as f throughout, u and v are interchanged as printed ('nouuelles', 'vn'), many words are broken or joined, and Google page banners ('Digitized by Google') and library stamps recur. No U+017F characters were present. SECOND WITNESS for exact wording (INTAKE scan-quality rule): usable to confirm that a sentence stands in the first printing, with the page image as the check; the 1881 edition is the quotable text. No public-domain English translation of Gilles exists (first pass searched).
